facts: Shiomisaki is famous as the southernmost tip of Honshu, the main island of Japan.
It is located in the town of Kushimoto within Wakayama Prefecture on the Kii Peninsula.
The iconic white Shiomisaki Lighthouse has offered panoramic ocean views and guided ships since 1873.
The cape is part of Yoshino-Kumano National Park, celebrated for its dramatic coastal geology and Pacific views.
The warm Kuroshio Current flows past the cape, creating a mild climate and rich marine biodiversity.
Nearby Hashigui-iwa features a striking natural row of around forty pillar-like rock formations stretching toward the sea.
Kushimoto is world-famous as the northernmost limit for thriving coral reefs in the Pacific Ocean.
Local restaurants serve exceptionally fresh seafood, especially Pacific bluefin tuna and bonito caught in local waters.
The area historically established Japan's strong cultural bond with Turkey after a famous naval rescue in 1890.
The Ertugrul Frigate Museum nearby honors the Turkish sailors rescued by local Kushimoto villagers during a storm.
A vast grassy plaza atop the cape hosts an annual festival where the winter grass is ceremoniously burned.
Runners can enjoy sweeping three-hundred-degree views of the Pacific Ocean horizon from the cape's grassy plateau.
Ancient Kumano Kodo pilgrimage routes pass through the surrounding mountains, attracting walkers and runners worldwide.
Strong ocean breezes make the cape a favorite spot for coastal weather watching and sea bird observing.
The region experiences frequent typhoons, earning it a reputation as a front line for tracking ocean weather systems.
Visitors can climb to the top of the historical lighthouse for an elevated view over the rugged coast.
The coastline is designated as part of the Nanki Kumano Geopark due to its unique geological features.
Kumano's holy mountains and coastal shrines have inspired spiritual journeys for over a thousand years.
